title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Notational slip: 'T = Ŷ − T' should read T = Ŷ \ Y (the set of punctures of Y).

The claim 'X → Y lui-même étale' is only partly legible. If it is the intended reading, it is correct for composites of étale maps and open immersions, but X → Y is then étale and not finite. This is precisely why the ramification points of X̂ → Ŷ lying over Y must be put into S.
No mathematical error otherwise. The page records an obstruction (non-canonical factorization, on the next page) rather than proving a result.

ideas.what: Adding open immersions ('bouchage des trous', i.e. erasing punctures) to the category of finite étale maps between open curves, on the surface side and the moduli side
ideas.modern_name: Point-erasing (forgetful) morphisms M_{g,n+1} → M_{g,n} in the Teichmüller tower; Birman exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984) for the tower; developed by Lochak, Schneps, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (1990s)
ideas.where_published: The Teichmüller tower and its basic operations are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); unsure whether 'bouchage de trous' appears verbatim there

ideas.what: Closing the category under composition forces general morphisms X → Y that are étale but not finite, given by squares X ⊂ X̂ → Ŷ ⊃ Y with S ⊃ f^{-1}(T), possibly strictly
ideas.modern_name: Category of hyperbolic curves with dominant étale morphisms (finite étale composed with open immersions); compactified covers with extra marked points, as in Hurwitz spaces with additional unramified markings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in anabelian geometry (e.g. Mochizuki, Tamagawa) and Hurwitz space theory

ideas.what: Decomposition of the puncture set S = S_0 ∪ S_1, with S_0 = preimage of T and S_1 containing both ramification points over Y and arbitrary unramified extra points
ideas.modern_name: Branch locus versus marked points in admissible or Hurwitz covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (Hurwitz, Fulton, Harris–Mumford for admissible covers)

missed.claim: Grothendieck pinpoints an obstruction to extending the profinite Galois–Teichmüller category to point-erasing morphisms. Up to isotopy, a morphism (étale composed with hole-filling) has no canonical factorization, so he cannot interpret the resulting classes via profinite completions of topological fundamental groups. He leaves this unresolved here.
missed.quote: Mais on est confronté, pour élargir la catégorie en conséquence, par l'impératif de pouvoir composer les morphismes ... à envisager des morphismes X → Y qui s'insèrent dans un diagramme commutatif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Defining a profinite or anabelian 'Galois–Teichmüller category' that includes both covers and point-erasure, with a good isotopy notion and Gal(Q̄/Q)-action, is close to questions on GT acting on the full Teichmüller tower (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura) and on the étale site of hyperbolic curves (Mochizuki). The explicit factorization-non-uniqueness obstruction is a modest but concrete historical detail.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine set-up: closing a category of covers under composition with open immersions, and noting that the punctures must include ramification points and extra unramified points. Point-erasing maps in the Teichmüller tower are well known from the Esquisse and later work. The only mildly notable item is his recorded difficulty (no canonical factorization up to isotopy, on the next page), a small unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'T = Ŷ - T' is as written, but intended T = Ŷ \ Y.
The parenthesis reads roughly '(étale finis, de types (bouchage de trous) et d'inclusion ouverte)', i.e. composing finite étale morphisms with hole-filling or open-inclusion morphisms.
'X → Y lui-même ...' is followed by an illegible word, plausibly 'étale' or 'il a ...'; uncertain.
The diagram label is (24) (written as '(2?)' in the image); its vertical arrows are X → Y and X̂ → Ŷ.
'X̂|T' denotes the inverse image of T in X̂.

The last lines should read approximately: 'le fait que X̂/Ŷ puisse avoir des [pts de ramification] ... l'on est obligé d'adjoindre non seulement les pts de ramification effective [et] les pts de X̂|T, mais aussi un des pts de S qui ne sont pas dans X̂|T'.
The archival page number in the margin is 17.
